correction.rejected_reading: CG 53469 was previously tentatively treated as a parallel for gilded toenail covers because footnote 28 appeared immediately after discussion of feet in a search snippet.
correction.correct_footnote_alignment: In the full paragraph structure, note 27 supports gold plates on fingers and toes of Horuta; note 28 follows the next sentence, 'Another golden phallus sheath was found in Tell Ibn es-Salam (Mendes)', and cites Vernier 1927, p.459, no.53469, pl.LXXXVII.

met_nesbanebdjedet_range.record: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Shabti inscribed for Nesbanebdjedet
met_nesbanebdjedet_range.statement: The chamber beneath contained a mummy adorned with trappings of gold leaf; see Cairo CG 53465-53469.

naville_topographic_control.work: Ahnas el Medineh, chapter on Mendes
naville_topographic_control.statement: The two mounds under the collective name Tmei el Amdid represent two different cities; the southern mound, now Tell Ibn es Salam, is associated with Thmuis, while the Mendes mound is distinct.

provenance_conflict.A: Met: CG 53465-53469 cross-reference attached to Nesbanebdjedet burial at Tell el-Rub'a/Mendes.
provenance_conflict.B: Modern phallus-sheath article: CG 53469 via Vernier p.459/pl.LXXXVII described as from Tell Ibn es-Salam (Mendes).
provenance_conflict.C: Naville: Tell Ibn es-Salam is the southern mound corresponding to Thmuis, geographically distinct from the Mendes mound.
possible_explanations: The modern article may use Mendes loosely for the district/paired archaeological area while preserving an older Tell Ibn es-Salam label.
The modern article may contain a site-name error while the CG number is correct.
Met's range cross-reference may group gold trappings broadly and require item-by-item verification.
A historical catalogue/Journal d'Entree nomenclature may use older collective place naming that later scholarship separates more strictly.
